module_title: Marketing Your Event Services on a Small Budget

lessons.title: Taking good photos of your decor using a smartphone
lessons.body:
You do not need an expensive camera to get clients. A mid-range smartphone like a Tecno Spark or Samsung Galaxy A series can take photos good enough for WhatsApp, Facebook, and flyers. The trick is light and angles. Always shoot during the day, near a window or outdoors in shade. Never use flash directly on decorâit creates harsh shadows. If you must shoot at night, use two or three battery-powered LED lights (cost: 5,000â10,000 Naira or 100â200 KES each) placed at 45-degree angles from the decor. 

Before taking a photo, clear the background. Remove buckets, plastic bags, or your own bag. Use a plain wall, a curtain, or a clean tablecloth as backdrop. For table settings, shoot from a slight angle above (45 degrees) to show height. For backdrops and arches, stand directly in front and shoot straight on. Take at least 10 shots per setup: wide, medium, and close-up of details like flower arrangements or name cards. 

Edit with free apps: Snapseed (Android/iOS) or Lightroom Mobile (free version). Adjust brightness slightly up, shadows down, and add a touch of warmth (temperature +5). Do not over-editâclients want to see what they will get. Crop to square for Instagram or WhatsApp status, and keep a horizontal version for Facebook. 

Save photos in folders by event type: weddings, birthdays, corporate. Name files clearly: âWedding_Backdrop_June2025.jpgâ. When sending to clients, send 3â5 best photos, not 20. Use WhatsAppâs âdocumentâ option to send without compression, or use Google Drive links. If you have a laptop, back up to a free Google Photos account (15GB free). 

Finally, practice. Take photos of your own home setup or a friendâs party. Compare with professional photos online and see what you can improve. Good lighting and a clean background are 80% of the work.

lessons.title: Creating a free business profile on WhatsApp Business and Facebook
lessons.body:
WhatsApp Business is free and turns your personal number into a storefront. Download it from Google Play or App Store. Set up your profile: business name (e.g., âGrace Events & Decorâ), category (Event Planner), address (your area, e.g., âKibera, Nairobiâ or âWuse, Abujaâ), and business hours. Add a profile photoâyour logo or a clear photo of your best decor. Write a description: âWe plan and decorate weddings, birthdays, and corporate events. Free consultation. Call 0803XXXXXXX.â 

Use the catalog feature to list services with prices: âWedding backdrop â from 50,000 Nairaâ, âBirthday table setup â from 20,000 Nairaâ. Add 5â10 photos per service. Set a greeting message: âHello! Thanks for contacting Grace Events. Please tell us your event date, location, and budget. Weâll reply within 1 hour.â Set a quick reply for âpriceâ that sends your catalog link. 

For Facebook, create a free Business Page (not a personal profile). Go to facebook.com/pages/create. Choose âLocal Businessâ or âEvent Plannerâ. Add profile and cover photos (cover: your best decor, 820x312 pixels). Fill in the About section with the same description, plus your WhatsApp link (wa.me/234803XXXXXXX). Invite friends to like the page. Post 3 times a week: a photo of recent work, a tip (â5 ways to save on wedding decorâ), and a client testimonial. Use free tools like Canva to make simple graphics. 

Link WhatsApp to Facebook: in WhatsApp Business settings, tap âBusiness Toolsâ > âFacebook Pageâ and connect. Now your WhatsApp button appears on your page. Also create a free Google Business Profile (google.com/business) so you appear in local searches. 

Keep it simple. Update your status daily with a photo or short video. Reply to messages within 1 hourâclients often choose the first responder. No need for a website yet; WhatsApp and Facebook are enough to start.

lessons.title: Asking satisfied clients for testimonials and referrals
lessons.body:
After an event, wait 2â3 days for the client to rest, then send a WhatsApp message: âHello [Name], thank you for trusting us with your [event]. Weâd love to know how you felt about the decor. Could you send a short voice note or text we can share? It helps us get more clients.â If they agree, ask specific questions: What did you like most? How was our communication? Would you recommend us? 

Record their voice note and transcribe it into text for flyers. Or ask them to write 2â3 sentences. Offer a small incentive: a 5% discount on their next event or a free centerpiece. For referrals, say: âIf you refer a friend who books us, you get 10% off your next event, and they get 5% off.â Track referrals in a notebook or free Google Sheet: client name, referred by, date, discount given. 

Post testimonials on your WhatsApp status, Facebook page, and in your catalog. Use a free app like Canva to make a simple graphic with the clientâs words and a photo of their event. Always ask permission before posting. If they prefer anonymity, use initials and event type: âA. from Lagos, wedding, June 2025â. 

For video testimonials, ask them to record a 30-second clip on their phone. Send them three questions in advance so they feel prepared. Keep it authenticâno script. 

Follow up with a thank-you message and remind them of the referral offer. A happy client is your best marketer. One wedding can lead to three more if you ask. Make it a habit: after every event, send a feedback request and a referral card (digital or printed).

lessons.title: Printing simple flyers and business cards at local print shops
lessons.body:
You do not need a professional designer. Use Canva (free) on your phone or a local cyber cafÃ©. Choose a flyer template (A5 size, 148x210mm). Replace text with your business name, services, phone number, and WhatsApp link. Use one strong photo of your decor as background. Keep text short: âWeddings | Birthdays | Corporate. Decor from 30,000 Naira. Call 0803XXXXXXX.â Save as PDF. 

For business cards, use a standard size (85x55mm). Include name, title, phone, WhatsApp, email, and one line: âEvent Planning & Decorâ. Use the same colors as your flyer. Canva has free templates. 

Go to a local print shop (in markets like Computer Village in Lagos, or River Road in Nairobi). Ask for prices: A5 flyers, 100 copies, full color, one side: around 3,000â5,000 Naira (or 500â800 KES). Business cards, 100 copies: 1,500â2,500 Naira (or 300â500 KES). Always ask for a sample print before paying for the full batch. Check for color accuracy and cut quality. 

Print 100 flyers and 100 cards to start. Distribute flyers at community events, churches, mosques, salons, and grocery stores. Ask permission first. Leave cards with vendors who serve your target clients: cake bakers, tailors, photographers. 

Keep a digital copy of your flyer to send on WhatsApp. When someone asks for details, send the PDF. Update your flyer every 6 months with new photos and prices. Do not overspendâstart small and reprint as needed.

lessons.title: Attending community events to network and show your work
lessons.body:
Community eventsâweddings, church bazaars, school fundraisers, market days, and cultural festivalsâare free networking opportunities. Find them on local radio, WhatsApp community groups, or by asking neighbors. Attend with a small display: a folding table, a few decor samples (a centerpiece, a name card, a fabric swatch), and your flyers and business cards. Wear a branded T-shirt if you have one. 

Arrive early and offer to help set up. This shows your skills and work ethic. Talk to organizers: âI noticed your stage could use a backdrop. I can set one up for free in exchange for a mention.â Many will agree. Bring a friend to take photos of your display and you working. Post those photos on WhatsApp and Facebook the same day. 

Collect phone numbers. Ask: âWhat events do you have coming up? May I send you my catalog?â Use a notebook or your phoneâs contacts. Follow up within 48 hours with a WhatsApp message: âGreat meeting you at [event]. Hereâs my catalog. Let me know if I can help with your next event.â 

Offer a free mini-workshop: â3 tips for decorating on a budget.â Speak for 10 minutes at a community meeting. This positions you as an expert. Bring a sign-up sheet for a free consultation. 

Network with other vendors: caterers, photographers, DJs. They can refer clients to you. Agree on a referral fee (5â10%). 

After the event, send a thank-you message to the organizer. Ask if you can be listed as a recommended vendor. Attend at least two events per month. Consistency builds trust and word-of-mouth.

lessons.title: Offering discounts for off-peak dates and repeat clients
lessons.body:
Off-peak dates are times when demand is low: weekdays (MondayâThursday), January to March, and rainy season months. Offer 15â20% off for events on these dates. Advertise: âBook a Tuesday wedding and save 20%.â This fills your calendar and keeps cash flowing. 

For repeat clients, create a simple loyalty card: after 3 bookings, they get 10% off the fourth. Or offer a free add-on: âBook your second event with us and get free table numbers.â Track clients in a notebook or Google Sheet. 

Announce discounts on WhatsApp status, Facebook, and at community events. Use a deadline: âOffer valid until [date].â This creates urgency. For off-peak, target clients who are flexible: small birthday parties, corporate trainings, baby showers. 

Calculate your costs first. If a full-price event costs 50,000 Naira and you discount 20%, you get 40,000. Ensure that still covers materials, transport, and labor. Do not discount below cost. 

For repeat clients, send a personal message on their anniversary or a month before their usual event: âHello [Name], as a valued client, you get 15% off your next booking. Letâs plan early.â 

Bundle services: âBook decor and planning together and save 10%.â This increases your average sale. 

Keep records of which discounts work. If a discount brings many bookings, repeat it. If not, try a different offer. Always ask for a testimonial after a discounted eventâthey are often happy to give one. 

Finally, do not compete on price alone. Emphasize quality and reliability. A small discount with great service beats a big discount with poor service.

quiz.q: What is the best time of day to take photos of your decor using a smartphone?
options: B) During the day near a window or in shade
C) At noon under direct sunlight
D) In a dark room with no light
quiz.explanation: Natural daylight near a window or in shade gives soft, even lighting without harsh shadows.

quiz.q: Which free app is recommended for editing smartphone photos of decor?
quiz.explanation: Snapseed is a free mobile app for basic photo editing like brightness and warmth.

quiz.q: How many photos should you send to a potential client?
quiz.explanation: Sending 3â5 best photos keeps the client focused and avoids overwhelming them.

quiz.q: What is a good background for decor photos?
options: B) A plain wall or clean tablecloth
quiz.explanation: A plain background makes the decor stand out without distractions.

quiz.q: What should you do before taking a photo of a table setting?
options: B) Remove buckets, bags, and clutter
quiz.explanation: Clearing clutter ensures the photo looks professional and focused on the decor.

quiz.q: Which app is used to create a free business profile for messaging?
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp Business is a free app specifically for business profiles and catalogs.

quiz.q: What feature in WhatsApp Business lets you list services with prices?
quiz.explanation: The catalog feature allows you to showcase services and prices directly in the app.

quiz.q: Where do you create a free Facebook Business Page?

quiz.q: What should you include in your WhatsApp Business greeting message?

quiz.explanation: A greeting that asks for key details helps you respond efficiently and professionally.

quiz.q: How often should you post on your Facebook Business Page?
quiz.explanation: Posting 3 times a week keeps your page active and visible without overwhelming you.

quiz.q: What incentive can you offer for a referral?

quiz.q: Where should you post client testimonials?

quiz.q: What is a good way to track referrals?
options: B) In a notebook or Google Sheet

quiz.q: Which free tool can help you design a flyer?

quiz.q: What is a good way to network at community events?
